purpose: Keep a public repository's human and agent entry surfaces distinct, bounded, and testable.
authority_ceiling: presentation and navigation only; this standard does not grant release, correctness, proof, provider-call, source-mutation, or publication authority

README.md.job: Answer what this is, why it matters, what is actually established, what remains unestablished, and the shortest way to inspect or run it.
first_screen: a concrete description without assumed project history
the principal result or runnable witness
two or more resolving routes for the reader
rules: Lead with concrete nouns, results, and commands; do not lead with internal ontology.
Treat reader attention as scarce: route detail to owned documents instead of copying inventories.
Do not use vague praise, readiness language, or sales claims as substitutes for evidence.
Keep install or build instructions executable and copyable.
A README is not agent policy, proof authority, or a release receipt.

AGENTS.md.job: Name the first correct action, authority boundaries, mutation order, owner routes, and proportional validation.
first_screen: an immediate pointer back to README.md for people
a task-shaped first action or bounded first-read route
rules: Route to generated inventories and owner documents; do not duplicate component catalogues.
Put commands, owners, stop conditions, prohibited actions, and validation where an agent can act on them.
Keep the complete file below 32768 bytes unless a repository-specific checker documents and enforces a stricter ceiling.
Provider-specific files are thin adapters to AGENTS.md and add no competing authority.
An agent entry file is not a human product pitch or a documentation archive.

external_basis: GitHub README guidance: README files communicate why a project is useful, what users can do with it, and how to get started.
GitHub repository guidance: README, license, citation, contribution, security, and support surfaces have distinct jobs.
OpenAI AGENTS.md guidance: AGENTS.md provides persistent repository context, commands, style, and testing instructions to coding agents.
